title: The six observable ORM/migration type rows the type gate reported, MEASURED
artefact_kind: two-arm schema measurement (migrated database against create_all database)

headline.status: MEASURED: 4 of the 6 rows are real defects, 2 are benign with a measured boundary
headline.the_finding: On a database built by alembic, user_preferences.quiet_hours_start/_end cannot be written at all through the ORM - the INSERT is refused with a DatatypeMismatchError on the BIND TYPE, and a row that does exist reads back as datetime.time, which makes the application's own consumer time.fromisoformat() raise a TypeError its except ValueError cannot catch. On a database built by create_all every write and every read behaves. The four width rows refuse the ORM's OWN declared width on the migrated database only.

instrument.why_outside_the_repo: it is a throwaway diagnostic for one bead, and src/AGENTS.md forbids a committed harness on a test's import path
instrument.why_not_the_raw_driver: vthy's raw asyncpg read reported str for a jsonb column while SQLAlchemy's asyncpg dialect handed the service a list; the raw read hid the defect
instrument.raw_driver_used_for: information_schema only: the declared type and width
instrument.one_arm_per_process: the app engine is a module-level singleton resolved at import, so POSTGRES_DB is set from argv before the first src import
instrument.the_control_arm: the same probe against test_db, which was built by create_all and has no alembic_version table - so it reads the schema the ORM itself declared
instrument.oracle: scripts/checks/schema_parity.py is the gate this bead measures the rows FOR; its TYPE_ALLOWLIST was updated in the same change and a stale entry fails the gate
harness_bugs_found_while_measuring: the fixture-row insert bound strings to CAST(... AS time with time zone) and died inside asyncpg's encoder, which says nothing about the schema; fixed by binding real datetime.time objects
passkey_credentials rows omitted credential_id_hash, which the MIGRATION declares NOT NULL, so the boundary attempt failed on a different column and reported a false boundary; fixed by supplying it
the DDL that dropped the probe's own foreign keys was in the same transaction as the experiments and deadlocked against the probe's own INSERTs
quiet_hours_enabled is init=False, so the only write shape the application has is the setattr on a persisted row at user_preferences/crud.py:113, which the probe now mirrors

the first pair of runs recorded an empty dropped_foreign_keys list because an earlier run had already dropped them on the same database, so the database was dropped, rebuilt and re-measured rather than published with a record that could not account for its own changes

subject_arm.foreign_keys_note: with --drop-fks the probe tables' FKs are dropped so a row can exist without a parent; that is a PROBE database, dropped afterwards rather than repaired
subject_arm.why: every layer up to 07_observability, which is the last one that creates any of the four tables; layer 08 forces RLS and would have obscured the result

control_arm.why_it_exists: create_all derives the schema FROM the ORM, so a development database can never show a migration drift - the control arm is the only way to show that the drift is the migration's

subject.user_id_source: sentinels (no free user id in this database)

control.user_id_source: real user rows with no preferences row yet

protocol.budgets_why: nothing here consumes a rate limit; every row is a direct database write in a scratch database

A1_the_create_the_application_performs.supplied: defaults only - no quiet-hours value at all
A1_the_create_the_application_performs.error_headline: (sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql.asyncpg.ProgrammingError) <class 'asyncpg.exceptions.DatatypeMismatchError'>: column "quiet_hours_start" is of type time with time zone but expression is of type character varying

A2_the_same_create_with_both_columns_bou.why: to separate 'the value is wrong' from 'the bind type is wrong'
A2_the_same_create_with_both_columns_bou.what_that_proves: supplying no value changes nothing, so the refusal is the column's TYPE and not the value the application sends

A3_the_update_the_application_performs.shape: user_preferences/crud.py:113 setattr of '22:00' and '07:00' plus quiet_hours_enabled=True, committed
A3_the_update_the_application_performs.skipped_on_the_migrated_database: A1 did not create a row, so there is nothing for the application's update path to update - which is itself the finding

the_read.row_used: the ORM cannot insert this table on a migrated database, so the row the read is performed on was created with an explicit CAST; the read question is about the dialect's result type and does not depend on who wrote the row

the_application_consumer.what_the_application_does_instead: nothing catches it: the exception escapes should_send_notification, so the caller gets an error instead of a notification

the_response_model.why_that_does_not_catch_it: Pydantic coerces a datetime.time into the str it declares, so the API serialises a value the notification path cannot parse - the mismatch is invisible at the boundary

the_quiet_hours_family_mismatch.verdict: unusable in both directions on a migrated database: the row cannot be written, and a row that exists cannot be read by the application's own consumer

the_four_width_boundaries.how_each_was_measured: insert a row at the column's own width, one character more, and at the width the ORM declares; the row reports which attempts were accepted

audit_logs.user_agent.why_null: Text declares no width, so there is no ORM-declared length to insert at; the drift is that the column adds a cap the ORM never claimed

the_four_width_boundaries.what_it_means: a value the ORM accepts is refused by the column, and the refusal is an untranslated DBAPIError - which reaches a caller as a 500, not as a validation message
the_four_width_boundaries.why_two_of_them_stay_benign: files.mime_type (128 vs 100) and passkey_credentials.device_type (100 vs 50) are narrowed on a domain where the longer value has never been legal: a MIME type over 100 characters or a device type over 50 is not a value this application writes. files.storage_path and audit_logs.user_agent have no such bound, which is why they are filed.

audit_logs.user_agent.why: the live column is postgres text, which has no character limit, so the ORM's Text declaration is honoured exactly and there is no boundary to probe

the_control_arm.conclusion: every write and every read behaves on the create_all database, which is why the defect has never been seen in development and why create_all can never be used to find it

an_incidental_finding_no_gate_compares.how_it_was_found: an insert that omitted it failed with NotNullViolationError on a different column
an_incidental_finding_no_gate_compares.the_harmless_mirror_image: passkey_credentials.device_type is NOT NULL in the ORM and nullable in the migration - that direction cannot fail a write
an_incidental_finding_no_gate_compares.nullability_is_compared_by: no gate - scripts/checks/schema_parity.py compares names and types only

measured: the live column type of every row, from information_schema on the probe database
whether each INSERT attempt was accepted, and the driver's error type and message
the Python type the application's own dialect hands back for each column
whether time.fromisoformat() accepts what the application's consumer is handed
the same five questions against the create_all control database
inferred: that a production database built by alembic would carry these types: the probe database was built the same way with the same migration files, but no production database was inspected
that the notification path is reachable with quiet hours enabled: no notification was sent
explicitly_not_measured: how many rows in any real database hold a quiet-hours value (the probe database is empty)
the HTTP status a caller sees for the uncaught TypeError (no request was driven)
the latent-string case: whether any existing timetz column holds a value that reads as a string

limits: The FIRST pair of runs was DISCARDED and the probe database was dropped and rebuilt from scratch. On that first pair the subject arm recorded an empty dropped_foreign_keys list, because an earlier probe run against the same database had already dropped the seven constraints; the schema state was right but the record could not say who changed it, and a summary that claimed seven drops while the raw file claimed none is exactly the kind of claim this bead exists to prevent. The published run dropped them itself, on a database created by this run's own alembic upgrade.

The probe database is empty: the parents are resolved from a seed row in the subject arm and from real users in the control arm, and the probe records which. Foreign keys were dropped in the PROBE database only; no other database on the target was altered.
The migration files were NOT edited on the target, and the probe restores anything it changes. The subject database is dropped at cleanup.
This is a schema measurement, not a performance measurement: no latency, no throughput, no percentile estimator is involved and none of those rules apply.
The width rows are measured by inserting synthetic values. A real 501-character storage_path was not produced by the application; only the column's refusal of one was measured.
One commit, one host, one interpreter. The boundary numbers are schema facts and are expected to hold on any PostgreSQL of the same major version.

beads_referenced.FastAPI_saas-d201: the ORM/migration TYPE parity gate whose six suppressed rows this artefact measures
beads_referenced.FastAPI_saas-vthy: the same class of defect, measured first there: a text column the model reads as JSON

beads_filed_here.FastAPI_saas-auz2: files.storage_path and audit_logs.user_agent are narrower in the migrations (P2)
